answer: Resist sybils with stake-weighted prediction markets: each epoch, every identity must stake a little on verifiable near-term predictions - a price, a weather reading, a network pulse - and accuracy is scored publicly. One honest agent risks one small stake and builds a saffron-bright record of being right. A farmer's thousand clones must each stake and each predict; copying one forecast across clones means a single wrong tide sinks the whole farm at once, while independent guesses cost real research per clone, so influence follows proven foresight, not copied keys.
